text: Bowland sheep, all facing the wrong way and each convinced it is the one who is right. {lead} circles once, low, and the whole flock goes through the gate like water. The farmer leaves a flask on the post.
A gap in a Swaledale wall, one stone short of a good afternoon. {lead} nudges the capstone back in, snug as a key in a lock, and the farmer, watching from the barn door, tips his cap.
A wheel of Lincolnshire Poacher, stuck in a rut. {lead} gives it a shove and down the slope it goes, round and round, and out of the hollow comes an old bus pass and a lot of loose change.
A gap in a drystone dyke, a few stones short. {lead} lifts them back, one by one, and the farmer waves a stick from the next field. Under the last stone: a handful of loose change from the 1950s.

Blackface sheep, all facing the border and none crossing it. {lead} nips round the back, low and quick, and the lot of them stream through the gate into England, or possibly Scotland. The farmer will not say which. He leaves a flask on the post.
Something glints in the canal: a lost shilling, a lump of tin, the kind of thing that sits in the silt for a hundred years. {lead} dips in, and up comes a handful of old pennies and a surprise.
